newsitem.title: USA: US-Singapore pact seen step to opening Asia air.
newsitem.headline: US-Singapore pact seen step to opening Asia air.

text.p: The aviation accord reached between the United States and Singapore was seen by industry experts Thursday as a good, if small, first step to opening other Asian markets and perhaps eventually Japan.
The "open skies" pact with Singapore, reached Wednesday after two days of talks here, will allow airlines of both sides to fly without restrictions to and beyond each other's countries.

Transportation Secretary Federico Pena, announcing the pact, said: "This agreement initiates what we hope will be a series of open skies relationships with our partners in Asia," the world's fastest growing aviation market.
The United States has argued that the world is turning toward ending restrictions on aviation services and that countries that resist jeopardized being left behind.

But Japanese officials have argued that their existing accord with the United States was weighted in favor of the United States and an "open skies" pact would only increase the dominance of the U.S. mega-carriers.
Brookings' Winston said the benefits of global "open skies" will parallel the benefits of aviation de-regulation in the United States -- more competition and lower fares.
In holding talks with one country at time, Winston said, "the United States is going at it the only way it can. The long run goal is to get everybody."
